0.title: How the NHS-Galleri trial worked
0.caption: Design and main result of the NHS-Galleri trial. Numbers from Sasieni et al., NEJM, 2026. Press a number to step through it.
steps: 142,250 people aged 50–77 in England gave blood at up to three yearly visits.
They were randomised 1:1. One arm's samples were run through the Grail multicancer test; the other arm's were stored untested.
After three rounds and a further year of follow-up, stage III–IV cancer rates were no different (ratio 1.03, CI 0.92–1.14). Stage IV alone hinted at a benefit (0.86, upper bound 1.00).

1.title: How blinatumomab replaced two chemo cycles
1.caption: Design and main results of the AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 trial in high-risk childhood B-cell leukaemia. Numbers from Schrappe et al., NEJM, 2026.
steps: 709 children with newly diagnosed high-risk B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia were randomised after consolidation therapy.
One arm got two cycles of blinatumomab, an antibody that directs T cells against CD19; the other got two cycles of standard chemotherapy.
At interim analysis (median 2.9 years), four-year event-free survival was 83.0% vs 70.3% (HR 0.51); infections fell (23.9% vs 69.4%) but neurotoxicity rose (12.0% vs 3.2%).

2.title: How the B7-H3 conjugate beat topotecan
2.caption: Design and main results of the phase 3 TAISHAN-302 trial in relapsed small-cell lung cancer. Numbers from Zhao et al., NEJM, 2026.
steps: 451 patients whose small-cell lung cancer had returned after platinum chemotherapy entered the TAISHAN-302 trial.
They were randomised to tambotatug pelitecan, an antibody-drug conjugate aimed at B7-H3, or to topotecan, the long-standing standard.
At interim analysis, median survival was 13.3 vs 9.4 months (HR 0.46), progression-free survival 7.4 vs 2.8 months, and responses 59.1% vs 9.7%.

3.title: How 8-weekly HIV injections beat daily pills
3.caption: Design and main result of the LATA trial in adolescents with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa. Numbers from Bwakura-Dangarembizi et al., The Lancet, 2026.
steps: 476 virally suppressed 12- to 19-year-olds in Kenya, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe, with a median of almost 12 years on therapy, enrolled.
They were randomised to cabotegravir-rilpivirine injections every eight weeks or to the standard daily dolutegravir-based pill.
By week 96, virus rebounded in 2 on injections (0.9%) vs 15 on pills (6.4%): non-inferior, then superior, with similar serious side effects.
